$comment: Cases both editors must judge alike. Each case is a Kotlin source and the issues expected for it, sorted by start, end and code; offsets count UTF-16 code units. Each issue is a signal the DSL calls and HTML strings of the source read that the source does not declare, so the cases hold both editors to the same reads: which strings a call reads, and which are read as free strings. A case may also say what the host knows of the project: htmlDsl, true or false, whether streamlord-html is on the classpath, which the file's imports decide otherwise; core, false when streamlord-core is not; and foreign, the names of calls that are not Streamlord's, which the harness turns into where each call of those names starts, as the scanner finds the calls. The same source under different options sits side by side, so a cache that ignores the options fails.

cases.name: a signal read inside a Pebble comment in a patch's markup, which the browser reads as text
a signal read inside a Pebble comment in a Kotlin string, which the browser reads as text
an expression handed to a DSL call reads its signals
the same call is somebody else's without the DSL, and its string is no HTML
a file that imports the DSL, when the host knows it is missing, reads no helper
the same file when nothing says it is missing reads the helper
markup handed to a foreign call is read as a free HTML string
text handed to a foreign call is not HTML, so nothing is read
text handed to Streamlord's patchElements is markup, and read
an HTML argument a Streamlord call does not read is read as a free string
cases.source: fun f(gen: ServerSentEventGenerator, header: String) = gen.patchElements(header, "")

cases.name: a script is no HTML string, whatever it holds, so nothing is read
a helper reads its signal when the host knows the DSL is there
a helper in a file that imports nothing of the DSL is somebody else's
